headline: City win derby with 10 men as Haaland's goal draws scrutiny
paragraphs: Manchester City won 1-0 at Old Trafford despite having Phil Foden sent off, with Erling Haaland scoring the derby winner. The Guardian and BBC Sport separately report that Pro Ref judged the goal should not have stood, calling it an 'error of judgment,' and stood down VAR official Matt Donohue and his assistant for this weekend's Premier League fixtures. Sky Sports' Gary Neville said pressure is mounting on United manager Michael Carrick after the club's joint-worst Premier League start.

Arsenal will contact Pro Ref over a penalty decision from Saturday's 2-0 win at Sunderland, confirmed separately by BBC Sport and Sky Sports. Sky's Jamie Carragher said manager Mikel Arteta is 'becoming the Sir Alex Ferguson of the Premier League' for his criticism of the call. Separately, the Guardian, the only outlet covering it here, reported PSG's first Ligue 1 win of the season was unconvincing, with new signing Ferran Torres the standout while most teammates struggled for form.

At Liverpool, head coach Andoni Iraola said his forwards must do more to make his system work, per the Guardian, after an uninspiring draw against Fulham; Sky Sports' Paul Merson separately questioned Florian Wirtz's form. Both BBC Gossip and Transfermarkt, in separate write-ups, reported Bayern Munich are monitoring Wirtz while Liverpool are tracking Bournemouth's Rayan as a target for next summer, unconfirmed transfer talk rather than a done deal.
